blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 992
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/992
- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 992
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/992
- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 992
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/992
- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

- **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. - **Title**: gh-982 smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-982` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +327
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T18:04:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # Source-level guards read site/ browser scripts as TEXT (they are never executed by the
          # suite): restore the pristine app.js so the counters nyc injected do not break them.
          cp site/factory/app.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/site/factory/app.js"
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

## PR Description

Closes #982
### What changed
`detectFailedChecks` now handles failed check-run `details_url`s shaped `/actions/runs/N` (no `/job/M` suffix): it resolves the run's failed jobs via `github_get_workflow_run_jobs` and fetches each failed job's log, so `ci_failures.md`/`ci_failures_full.log` are produced for those checks instead of being silently skipped.

### Key decisions
- `/runs/N/job/M` URLs keep the existing direct job-log path — the run-jobs lookup only runs when no job id is in the URL
- Added `getWorkflowRunJobs(runId)` to the GitHub SCM provider in `js/common/scm.js`; `githubHelpers` guards with `typeof === 'function'` so GitLab/ADO providers are unaffected (their `details_url` shapes don't match `/runs/N` anyway)
- Tolerates `{jobs: [...]}` / `{job_runs: [...]}` / bare-array run-jobs responses (mirrors `js/common/ci.js` `_jobsOf`)
- Only jobs concluding `failure`/`timed_out` get logs fetched (matches the check-level filter); per-job log sections are labelled with the job name

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_githubHelpers.json   # 76 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 3652 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CHECK[Failed check-run] --> URL{details_url shape?}
  URL -->|/runs/N/job/M| JOB[Direct github_get_job_logs]
  URL -->|/runs/N| RUN[github_get_workflow_run_jobs]
  RUN --> FILTER[Filter jobs: failure / timed_out]
  FILTER --> LOGS[get_job_logs per failed job]
  JOB --> MD[ci_failures.md + ci_failures_full.log]
  LOGS --> MD
```

</details>

# gh-982: smAgent detectFailedChecks misses /runs/N-shaped check-run URLs (context-prep half-b of the CI-failures blindness)

## Description

Follow-up to #957 (closed): the rework-blindness root cause had two halves. Half (a) — dart bridge returning raw text for github_get_job_logs/gitlab trace/ado pipeline logs — is fixed by epam/dmtools-dart#429 (auto-releases to factories on merge; legs resolve DMTOOLS_VERSION=latest).

Half (b): js/common/githubHelpers.js detectFailedChecks (~line 510) extracts the job id only from details_url matching /actions/runs/N/job/M — check-run URLs shaped /actions/runs/N are skipped silently, so ci_failures_full.log is never even attempted for those. Live evidence 2026-10-17: dart legs got job ids fine; fa legs hit this gap historically. Fix: also accept /runs/N (fetch the run's failed jobs via github_get_workflow_run_jobs then get_job_logs per job).
